title: handleSubmitForApproval calls `loadMsa()` â€” function is not defined in the component scope
detail: Line 83: `loadMsa();` â€” but there's no function named loadMsa defined anywhere in the file. The component only has the inline useEffect at line 42-58 for initial load, no named load function. Calling loadMsa() will throw ReferenceError at runtime. Result: clicking 'Submit for Approval' on an MSA succeeds in the PATCH (line 81) and the audit write (line 82), then crashes on the refresh step, leaving the UI showing the OLD status. The user thinks the submit failed and may click again, double-submitting. P1 because this is a silent data-vs-UI divergence on a money-flow action.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:83 `loadMsa();` â€” grep 'function loadMsa' or 'const loadMsa' in this file returns zero hits. The file uses an inline useEffect with no named loader, so the closure has no loadMsa symbol.
recommendedFix: Two options: (a) extract the load logic into a useCallback named loadMsa (similar to CustomerDetail.jsx:42 pattern) and call it here, OR (b) replace line 83 with a re-fetch: `const fresh = await apiGet(...); setMsa(fresh);` â€” same pattern as handleSaveEdit line 101. Option (a) is cleaner. Also verify by triggering the submit action in Test.

title: MsaDetail destructures `isAdmin, isManager` but never uses them
detail: Line 28: `const { user, isAdmin, isManager } = usePortalUser();` â€” isAdmin and isManager are destructured but the MSA edit/generate actions are rendered unconditionally (no role guard at all). Either the role checks are missing (P1 cat 9, similar to CR-0248) or these imports are dead code. Given the MSA document is the entry point to all customer billing, it is plausible that edit should be admin-only.
evidence: MsaDetail.jsx:28 destructure; no other references to isAdmin/isManager in the file.
recommendedFix: Decide per business rule: are MSA edit/generate actions restricted to admins? If YES, wrap the Edit MSA button (line 137-139) and Generate MSA button (line 143-145) in `{isAdmin() && ...}`. If NO, drop the unused destructure.

title: DocumentHistory useEffect has no error handler on the apiGet
detail: Line 243-245: `apiGet(...).then(r => setDocs(r?.value ?? []));` â€” no .catch, so any failure (403 on dcfg_document_outputs, 500, timeout) produces an unhandled promise rejection. The panel silently shows 'No documents generated yet.' even when the table is just unreachable.
recommendedFix: Add `.catch(() => setDocs([]))` or surface the error to a toast/banner.
